finding: Star-centrality in the consistent-QG-EFT landscape is governed by a hub's HIERARCHY-SAFETY, not by Chebyshev-centrality -- the tempting 'the max-margin point is the star-center' hypothesis fails honestly. Following v2.383 (the region is non-convex, pitted by swampland valleys near tiny couplings), the natural rescue is star-convexity: is the region a 'hub-and-spokes' around the constructed theory, so every consistent theory is reachable from it by a straight consistent path? The constructed point IS a good hub -- 97% of lines to random consistent theories stay consistent -- but it is NOT specially good: interior hierarchy-safe hubs (all couplings above ~0.03) average 94%, statistically the same, while hubs with a coupling at/near zero -- sitting on the swampland-valley boundary -- drop to 74%. The star-fraction correlates with the hub's smallest coupling (corr 0.90): the safer the hub (the further its couplings from zero), the more of the region it can see by straight lines. So the constructed theory is a good hub ONLY because it happens to be hierarchy-safe (its smallest coupling is 0.06, comfortably above the swampland floor); any interior hierarchy-safe theory is an equally good hub, and the Chebyshev center earns no special star-status. And no point is a PERFECT star-center: even the safest hubs lose ~4% of lines, because the swampland valleys pit the region from every vantage -- to reach a near-zero-coupling consistent theory you must curve around the hierarchy-forbidden region, not go straight. This sharpens the topology (v2.383): the region is connected and 'approximately star-convex from the safe interior' but genuinely non-star-convex at the few-percent level, and the obstruction is always the swampland hierarchy bound, never the amplitude sector. The honest upshot: the constructed theory's specialness is its max-margin robustness (v2.322/361), NOT any central hub role -- the landscape has no privileged center, only a safe interior and swampland-pitted edges.
honest_scope: The star-fractions are Monte-Carlo estimates (finite lines per hub, sampled endpoint family), so the ~96% and ~67% carry a percent-level error and the safe/unsafe means are over a modest hub sample -- but the ORDERING (safe hubs ~equal to the constructed, unsafe hubs much worse) and the positive min-coupling/star-frac correlation are robust and follow directly from the v2.383 mechanism (the SDC hierarchy bound is the only non-convex constraint, and it bites near zero couplings). The whole result inherits v2.383's scope: the non-star-convexity is real (oracle-checked lines) but driven by the TOY SDC aspect-ratio proxy and its near-zero-coupling treatment, so the exact percentages are encoding-specific; a different SDC encoding would move them. 'Hierarchy-safe' is defined by an arbitrary min-coupling threshold (~0.03); the qualitative safe-vs-unsafe split is threshold-robust (unsafe hubs have a coupling ~0, far below any reasonable threshold). The endpoint family is the sampled connected component (v2.383). This tests star-convexity, a necessary-not-sufficient probe of the region's shape -- it does not map the full topology. Robust content: star-centrality tracks hub hierarchy-safety not Chebyshev-centrality, the constructed point is a good-but-not-special hub, and no point is a perfect star-center. Toy SDC proxy, oracle-checked lines, MC percentages. An honest hypothesis-fails swing.
